Let \(L_m=\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\dots,m)\), and set \(k=\lfloor \sqrt[3]{n}\rfloor\).

- If \(n=k^3\), then we need \(L_{k-1}\mid k^3\). For \(k\ge4\), Bertrand gives a prime \(p\) with \(k/2<p<k\), so \(p\mid L_{k-1}\) but \(p\nmid k^3\). Thus only \(k=1,2\) work, giving \(n=1,8\).

- If \(k^3<n<(k+1)^3\), then we need \(L_k\mid n\).  
  For \(k=7\), \(L_7=420\), and the only multiple of \(420\) in \([343,511]\) is \(420\), which works. For \(k\le6\), all such \(n\) are \(<420\).  
  For \(k\ge8\), \(L_k>(k+1)^3\), so no multiple of \(L_k\) lies in \([k^3,(k+1)^3)\).

Therefore the largest possible \(n\) is \(\boxed{420}\).
